children: Rajarshi Moitra on how a USD 85 million investment, a new Satellite Technology Centre and a local-for-local model are preparing the company for its centenary in 2031

Thirty years after arriving in India with a long-term commitment to quality, Bridgestone counts the country among its strategic growth markets. Two manufacturing plants, more than 4,000 dealers and a USD 85 million investment in Pune and Indore support a business that Rajarshi Moitra, managing director (MD), Bridgestone India, describes as local-for-local.

How would you describe the journey from a new entrant in 1996 to a core growth market for the Group, and what role does India play in Bridgestone's global plans as it approaches its 100th anniversary in 2031?

Bridgestone came to India in 1996 with a long-term commitment of contributing to Indian society with superior quality. The automotive sector was witnessing a revolution, with global brands entering the market and Indian brands investing in manufacturing infrastructure. This created an opportunity for us as we set up our first manufacturing plant in Pithampur, Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh.

Today, thirty years later, we are proud to be a very strong contributor to India's automotive development with our two manufacturing plants: one in Chakan, Pune, second at Pithampur, Dhar District in Madhya Pradesh and a country wide sales and service network to provide superior customer experience to our customers across segments. We take pride in our robust presence across the OE and aftermarket segments, spanning passenger cars, trucks and buses, and off-highway applications. We remain committed to delivering superior customer experiences through innovative products, services, and sustainable mobility solutions.

Bridgestone India has also been identified among the strategic growth markets for Bridgestone globally. India is the fastest-growing large economy, and we see strong potential to build on the foundation we have created.

The last thirty years has seen a transformation in the automotive industry, with India becoming a key manufacturing hub for global and local automotive players. We have grown alongside this evolution and built strong manufacturing, technology, distribution, and people capabilities in India. This has made us a formidable player in both the OEM and aftermarket across passenger, commercial and off highway segments.
How has Bridgestone blended Japanese practices with the Indian market's speed and diversity?

At Bridgestone India, we sit at a position of unique advantage where we are able to leverage our Japanese heritage of superior quality, discipline, and manufacturing excellence while having a deep understanding of the Indian consumer and culture. And that is what we bring through the four pillars of our foundation- ‘Seijitsu-Kyocho’ (Integrity and Teamwork), ‘Shinshu-Dokuso’ (Creative Pioneering), ‘Genbutsu-Genba’ (Decision-Making Based on Verified, On-Site Observations), and ‘Jukuryo-Danko’ (Decisive Action after Thorough Planning). These core principles remain consistent across Bridgestone operations globally and have been a key foundation for a successful business model in India.
Bridgestone has spoken about premium products, premium retail and customer experience, alongside growth in the aftermarket. What is driving growth today?

At Bridgestone our core mission is serving society with superior quality. Our tyres carry life and hence safety and quality is at the core of everything that we do. We constantly engage in ensuring that we provide high quality and safe tyres with superior technology to our consumers every single day.

Our products are delivered to our consumers and end-users through our very cherished Bridgestone retail network. Bridgestone's premium retail outlets offer well-trained personnel, state-of-the-art equipment, and advanced machinery. Because tyres are a low-involvement category with a notable knowledge gap, it is crucial that trusted experts guide customers toward the right selection based on their specific needs. Bridgestone develops trusted channel partners who can provide quality service and transparent advice to the customer. With the advent of technology, our endeavour is to leverage it as an accelerator for superior customer experience.

When it comes to channel infrastructure, we are converting the tyre purchase journey from a onetime engagement to a lifetime engagement through value creation for our consumers. The Bridgestone philosophy is about creating value for customers and society which is in line with our founder Shōjirō Ishibashi's statement - "I am convinced that a simple profit-seeking business will never thrive, but a business that contributes to its society and country will be forever profitable." That is the core of our company.
Bridgestone announced an investment of around USD 85 million in its Pune and Indore plants. What is the thinking behind this investment?

The investment is primarily focused at being ahead of the curve in terms of both our capacity and capability readiness to cater to the Indian consumer. A significant part of this capacity investment is being implemented in Pune for capacity and capability upgradation and as well as in Indore, where we are looking at upgrading our facilities to cater to the future consumer needs.

These efforts are expected to increase the Pune plant's total production capacity by approximately 1.1 million tyres annually by 2029. Bridgestone established a Satellite Technology Centre in India in 2025, aimed at accelerating product development and improving responsiveness to local market needs.
How does Bridgestone combine global research with local engineering, and what does "local-for-local" mean for the Indian market?

We follow the global quality benchmark, with deep understanding of Indian consumer requirements. Bridgestone India is a local for local operations with our products and services being developed, produced and managed completely locally and our future endeavour is to continue to be a local for local operations.

Over the past three decades, Bridgestone India has contributed to India's growth through investment, employment generation, manufacturing excellence, technology development, local sourcing, and skill development. We are proud with our contribution towards the growing MSME sector with our channel and supplier partnerships. I am glad to share that we are able to generate more than 15,000 employment opportunities through our partnerships.
How is the retail strategy changing as demand grows in Tier 2, 3 and 4 markets?

The company is expanding its distribution network to enhance the coverage and create a larger footprint across tier- 2, 3, 4 cities where rising incomes and infrastructure development are fuelling mobility demand. We have played a pioneering role in transforming the tyre retail experience in India since launching our flagship Select store format in 2008. Over the years, our premium Select network has set new benchmarks in customer experience, service quality, and retail excellence. As customer expectations continue to evolve, we remain focused on continuously innovating and enhancing the tyre buying journey across the country.

Today's customers access information, compare products, and expect the same customer experience as consumers in larger cities. This is where our retail strategy of enhancing customer experience comes into play. Our Select format is a step in that direction and a part of Bridgestone's ongoing commitment to enhance the tyre retail experience across India with innovative, customer-centric service offerings.

With the Pune plant being carbon neutral and Bridgestone working towards greater use of renewable and recycled materials, how are you approaching sustainability? And how are EVs changing tyre development?

Aligned with our founders' vision of serving society with superior quality - societal value is at the centre of everything that we do. At Bridgestone, we look at sustainability across the value chain, starting with: Manufacturing - Our Pune plant is carbon neutral and we have now announced that our plant in Indore will be carbon neutral by 2028. Products - We focus on ecosystem circularity and lower carbon footprints through advanced rolling resistance coefficients. We are also developing EV ready tyres like the Turanza 6i to be able to contribute to a sustainable future.

Dedicated to integrating sustainability into every aspect of our operations, our growth supports both economic progress and social well-being. Creating value for society is not just an initiative-it is a core part of our way of doing business. We will continue to conduct our business responsibly and contribute to a better future for generations to come.
As Bridgestone approaches its 100th anniversary in 2031, what will be the key priorities for India over the next five years?
Looking ahead, we are targeting to drive volume through strong market demand, while focusing on lasting customer relationships and product superiority.

Our main focus is to grow the business, continue serving society and build a future-ready organisation in terms of capabilities and culture. To achieve this, we are following a 5-pillar strategy: First is Product superiority with a strong localisation focus. Our world-class, premium products are built for India, for Indian consumers.

The second pillar is retail and channel expansion. Bridgestone currently operates a network of over 4,000 dealers, including around 900 exclusive "Bridgestone Select" outlets, and plans to expand this network while also bringing more technology enabled solutions. The third pillar is manufacturing capacity and capability building. Our plants are currently operating at optimum utilisation levels, and we are constantly evaluating investments to be future ready and to capture the future growth potential of India. The fourth pillar is to deliver a superior omni-channel customer experience. With the advent of AI, we expect information asymmetry to decrease and our consumers to become more informed. Therefore, there is a need to revamp the customer experience for this whole new world.

To deliver the above four priorities, we are also building a future ready organisation with strong and capable leadership. We believe that good company of people help us build good products and services and deliver good customer experience. As we move towards 2031, our goal is to make the next chapter of Bridgestone's India story as meaningful as the first 30 years and ensure that India becomes an even more important part of Bridgestone's global growth story.
